title: Tanvi Sharma, Unnati Hooda Set Up All-Indian Syed Modi Semi-Final in Lucknow
excerpt: Second seed Tanvi Sharma and third seed Unnati Hooda both came through three-game quarter-finals on Friday at the Syed Modi India International Super 300, guaranteeing India a women's singles finalist. Defending champions Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand also reached the women's doubles semi-finals.
body:
• Tanvi Sharma beat Indonesia's Ni Kadek Dhinda Amartya Pratiwi 21-19, 18-21, 21-14, and Unnati Hooda beat Anmol Kharb 21-19, 15-21, 21-18, in Friday's quarter-finals at the Syed Modi India International Super 300 in Lucknow.
  • The two Indians meet in Saturday's semi-final, so India is assured of a place in the women's singles final on Sunday, November 29.
  • Defending champions Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand advanced to the women's doubles semi-finals on a walkover and remain on course for a third straight title.
  • India's men's challenge ended on Friday with quarter-final defeats in singles and doubles.

India will have a finalist in the women's singles at the Syed Modi India International Super 300 after second seed Tanvi Sharma and third seed Unnati Hooda won three-game quarter-finals on Friday to set up an all-Indian semi-final at the Babu Banarasi Das Indoor Stadium in Lucknow. The tournament, part of the BWF World Tour, runs from November 24 to 29 with total prize money of $250,000.

Two three-game wins

Tanvi, the 17-year-old who won the Taipei Open Super 300 in August to become the youngest champion in that tournament's history, had to dig deep against Indonesia's Ni Kadek Dhinda Amartya Pratiwi. She took the opening game 21-19, dropped the second 18-21, and regained control in the decider to close it out 21-14.

Unnati's quarter-final was an all-Indian contest against Anmol Kharb that lasted one hour and 17 minutes. Unnati won 21-19, 15-21, 21-18, surviving a strong response from Kharb before closing out the match. She had also reached the semi-finals of the Taipei Open earlier this year.

In the other half of the draw, Japan's top seed Riko Gunji will face Thailand's fourth seed Supanida Katethong in the semi-finals. Gunji ended Tasnim Mir's run 21-11, 21-11; Tasnim had earlier stunned sixth seed Kirsty Gilmour of Scotland in the pre-quarterfinals.

Treesa and Gayatri's title defence continues

Top seeds Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, the defending women's doubles champions and World Championships bronze medallists from New Delhi in August, advanced to the semi-finals after French seventh seeds Margot Lambert and Camille Pognante conceded a walkover in the quarter-finals. The Indian pair, winners of the previous two editions of this tournament, are chasing a third consecutive title.

India also kept a mixed doubles presence in the last four. Sathwik Reddy Kanapuram and Reshika Uthayasooriyan beat compatriots Viraj Kuvale and Rutaparna Panda 21-8, 21-14, and will next face Malaysia's Wee Yee Hern and Vannee Gobi, who knocked out top seeds Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto on Thursday.

Men's challenge ends

Friday ended India's challenge in the men's events. In men's singles, Tushar Suveer lost 21-19, 19-21, 9-21 to Indonesia's Prahdiska Bagas Shujiwo after taking the opening game. In men's doubles, third seeds Hariharan Amsakarunan and MR Arjun won the opening game 21-10 but lost the next two 12-21, 13-21 to Thai seventh seeds Chaloempon Charoenkitamorn and Worrapol Thongsa-nga. Sai Pratheek K and Ruban Kumar Rethinasabapathi also lost, 22-20, 13-21, 9-21, to Indonesian top seeds Raymond Indra and Nikolaus Joaquin after winning the first game.

What's next

The semi-finals are played on Saturday, November 28, headlined by Tanvi against Unnati for a place in Sunday's women's singles final. Treesa and Gayatri continue their title defence in women's doubles, and Kanapuram and Reshika carry India's hopes in mixed doubles. The finals are on Sunday, November 29, in Lucknow.
